# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 55 (Bi-Vb Pc55)
**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc55
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 55
**Title (English, from literature):** Being stingy with families
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-pc55
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
As noted by Ute Hüsken, this ordinance serves to ensure that lay donors are not deprived of the opportunity to give alms and accrue religious merit, thereby maintaining harmonious relations between the monastic order and the laity [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the rule and its Vibhaṅga is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this rule was widely shared across early Buddhist monastic traditions, appearing in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (Pācittiya 55) and Bhikkhunī Parivāra, as well as in the Vibhaṅgas and Prātimokṣa sūtras of the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda (in Sanskrit), Sarvāstivāda, and Mūlasarvāstivāda recensions preserved in Chinese and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects extensive internal formulaic reuse with dozens of other Vinaya rules, particularly Bhikkhunī Saṅghādisesa 3 and Pācittiyas 25, 30, and 15 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also establishes cross-language alignments with Tibetan canonical Vinaya texts, including the Tibetan translation of the *Āryasarvāstivādimūlabhikṣuṇīpratimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4112) [DharmaNexus].
